E072-01.notes: Two independent clauses. A comma splice; B fused sentence; D 'and, it' has a misplaced comma after the conjunction. C semicolon joins them correctly.

E072-02.notes: A, C, D are all redundant (repeatedly = again and again / over and over / repeating himself). B is concise.

E072-03.notes: Generic list of adhesive uses is off-topic in the discovery narrative. A false (doesn't explain); B false (not about Silver's adhesive); C no contradiction.

E072-04.notes: Choir detail explains why Fry had a hymnal in sentence 5. B is the trap (it supports, not shifts, focus); C false; D not repeated.

E072-05.notes: Subject 'slips' is plural; past narrative ('realized' in 1974). A singular/present; B singular and wrong tense; D creates fragment clause with no finite verb.

E072-06.notes: Failure in test markets contrasted with success of free samples: contrast needed. B similarity, C cause-effect, D example are all illogical.

E072-07.notes: Register: A 'totally hooked', B 'like, obsessed', C 'went crazy' are all too informal. D is plain and conveys enthusiasm for the product.

E072-08.notes: Only B conveys widespread use. A vague; C packaging/variety; D manufacturing.

E072-09.notes: A ties back to the weak, seemingly useless adhesive from paragraph 1. B, C, D do not connect to the beginning.

E072-10.notes: Essay traces weak adhesive to Post-it Notes. A no chemistry detail; B choir is minor; D false - the Press 'n Peel failure is mentioned.

E072-11.notes: Two items joined by 'and' take no comma. A unnecessary comma; C comma after 'and'; D semicolon does not join independent clauses here.

E072-12.notes: Sentence 6 says 'That spring', needing a year; D supplies 1950 and introduces the real bear. A, B, C off-topic and leave 'That spring' unanchored.

E072-13.notes: General bear fact interrupts the rescue story. A, B false claims; D no contradiction (and not the real reason).

E072-14.notes: Pronoun is object of 'named' (officials named him Smokey), so 'whom'. A subject form; C 'him' makes the clause independent, creating an ungrammatical interrupter; D possessive is meaningless.

E072-15.notes: 'until 1976' requires simple past. A present, B future, D present perfect all clash with a completed past period.

E072-16.notes: D gives concrete evidence of fame (own ZIP code). A restates vaguely; B, C about zoo life, not recognition.

E072-17.notes: A, C, D redundant pairs. B concise.

E072-18.notes: Only C explains why 'forest fires' became 'wildfires' (some planned fires are beneficial). A, B, D do not address the reason for the change.

flags.note: Answer choices are not in ascending order (A=Sentence 3, B=Sentence 1, C=Sentence 6, D=Sentence 9); ACT lists placement options in passage order. Reorder for format consistency.

E072-19.notes: 'Its message' refers to the first poster in sentence 3, whose image (pouring water on a campfire) matches the message. Sentence 1 has no poster yet; sentence 6 is the rescue; sentence 9's slogan referent is not about campsites and would interrupt the conclusion.
